questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The restaurants and food scene of Sai Ying Pun's High Street
The history and haunted reputation of Hong Kong's old mental hospital
Baroque architecture in Hong Kong's colonial-era public buildings
Japanese occupation of Hong Kong and its wartime execution sites
questions.explain: It recounts the building's history, preservation and its haunted reputation.

questions.q: What was the building originally used for when completed in 1892?
options: Officers' barracks for the colonial Hong Kong garrison
Medical Staff Quarters of the Government Civil Hospital
Female wards of the Government Civil Hospital annex
Quarters for the Sai Ying Pun police and prison staff
questions.explain: It first served as the Medical Staff Quarters of the Government Civil Hospital.

questions.q: What was preserved in the redevelopment?
options: The whole original building, restored in full
Only the L-shaped granite facade and verandas
The roof and the female patient wards intact
The original gardens and the interior staircases
questions.explain: Only the L-shaped granite facade and verandas on the High Street side were preserved intact.

questions.q: Which bus passes directly in front of the Old Mental Hospital?
options: The 12 green minibus
The 10 green minibus
The 103 bus
The 31 green minibus
questions.explain: The 12 green minibus passes right in front, on a circular route.

questions.q: What does the passage suggest about the wartime execution stories?
options: They are well documented in colonial-era records
They are rumours rather than established fact
They were disproved by archaeologists' excavations
They concern only the neighbouring memorial park
questions.explain: It says the site was 'purportedly' used for executions and the mass grave was 'rumoured'.
